subject.title: fix(telegram): show progress for queued replies

question: Should queued-follow-up admission and settlement remain a shared dispatcher lifecycle contract, with Telegram using it to reset and clean up ephemeral progress UI after final delivery paths complete?
rationale: The patch is focused and proven for Telegram, but the new callback pair changes the shared runner’s channel lifecycle surface and future channel behavior; that boundary choice needs owner intent rather than contributor follow-up.

options.title: Confirm the shared lifecycle seam
options.body: Accept the optional admission and settlement callbacks as the canonical channel-presentation boundary and merge after normal current-head checks.

options.title: Narrow the design first
options.body: Replace or constrain the shared callback contract if maintainers want queued presentation cleanup to remain channel-specific or tied to a different delivery boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm the shared lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Accept the optional admission and settlement callbacks as the canonical channel-presentation boundary and merge after normal current-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent auto-reply delivery-semantics history is the strongest available routing signal for the shared runner contract.
